PendingOut.description: What a person is asked to approve, so the screen needs no step parsing.
PendingOut.title: PendingOut

get.description:
What is left before a limit: asks on the shared default key today, unfinished
runs against the cap, whether you saved your own key, and open live streams.
The limits are yours, not per workspace; `workspace` only checks that it is
one you may use (404 otherwise) and is echoed back. Read only.

Your runs, newest first unless `ordering` says otherwise (`created_at` or
`latency_ms`, `-` for descending). Filter by `status` (repeat it for several),
`q` (text in the question) and `created_after` / `created_before`. `meta.count`
is the number of runs that match.

post.description:
Start a run on the demo, or on one of your own workspaces (`workspace`).
The agent plans and proposes SQL, then waits for approval; follow it on
`/runs/{id}/events`. One run counts as one spend of the shared default key.
Runs on your own workspace are kept out of eval data.

get.description: A run and its steps. Poll this when the live stream is not available.

post.description: Run the SQL the agent proposed. Only while the run waits for approval.
End a paused run without running anything.

Run your own SQL instead. It goes through the same guard; a refusal is a 400
and the run stays paused.

get.description:
Server-sent events: `step` for each step, then one `status` event when the
run pauses for approval or ends. Event ids are step indexes; reconnect with
`Last-Event-ID` to continue. Over the open-stream limit it answers 429
`agent_stream_limit`: poll `GET /runs/{id}` instead.

The stored trace in order. No model call and no query on the demo database:
it is read from the steps alone.

The rows of a succeeded run, up to the row cap. Rows are not stored: this
runs the run's stored SQL again, through the guard, on the read-only
connection. It never takes SQL from the request, so the numbers can differ
from the first run if the data changed. 409 `run_not_succeeded` otherwise.

post.description:
Answer a question about the demo database, or about one of your own
workspaces (`workspace`): the SQL that ran, the result table and a confidence
score. The SQL is checked before it runs and runs on the read-only connection
of that workspace only.

get.description:
Every dependency the backend needs. Not wrapped in the envelope, so
uptime checks can read `status` directly; 503 when anything fails.

The signed-in user's saved keys: provider, last four characters, model.
The key itself is never returned.

put.description: Check the key with the provider and save it encrypted.

get.description:
The signed-in user, or 401. The frontend's route guards use this.

Also sets the csrftoken cookie (signed in or not): the app calls this
first on every load, so its first POST already has a token to send.

Every table of the demo schema, or of your workspace (`workspace`), with
columns, keys, comments and row estimates. Send `If-None-Match` with the last
`ETag` to get a 304 when nothing changed.

One table, same shape as in the full schema. An unknown name is a 404
`table_not_found` that says nothing else about the schema.

The shared demo workspace first, then your own, with table counts and bytes
used. `meta.max_workspaces` is the cap.

post.description:
Create a private workspace: an empty schema only you and your agent can
reach. `workspace_limit_reached` when you already have the maximum.

delete.description: Always refused: the shared demo workspace cannot be deleted.

patch.description: Always refused: the shared demo workspace is read-only for everyone.

delete.description:
Drop the workspace's schema, tables and login roles for good. Your past
agent runs stay in your history and can still be replayed.

get.description:
One of your workspaces. Someone else's workspace is a 404, the same as a
missing one.

post.description:
Relate a child table's column(s) to a parent table's primary key or unique
column(s), both in this workspace. Existing rows are checked: the first row
with no parent is named in a 409 `constraint_violation`.

Run your own SQL on your own workspace: full control inside the schema
(CREATE, ALTER, DROP, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT, views, indexes, several
statements). The whole request is one transaction: any failing statement
rolls everything back and answers 422 `sql_failed` with the Postgres code and
message. Transaction control and COPY are refused (`sql_invalid`); a request
that makes the workspace bigger than its cap is rolled back with
`workspace_full`. Structural statements are logged; the agent sees them on its
next read.

get.description: The workspace's tables with their columns, including the hidden `_row_id`.

post.description:
Create an empty table from a column spec. It gets a hidden identity key
`_row_id`. `table_limit_reached` / `column_limit_reached` name the cap.

delete.description: Drop the table and its rows for good, with relations that point at it.

patch.description: Rename a table and/or set its description.

post.description: Add a column. A NOT NULL column on a table that has rows needs a default.

delete.description:
Drop a column (and the keys and relations that use it). The last column
cannot be dropped.

patch.description:
Rename a column, set its description or nullability, or change its type. A
retype converts every value inside one transaction; a value that does not
convert is a 422 `cast_failed` naming its row id, and nothing changes.

put.description:
Make these columns the table's primary key (replacing any earlier one).
Existing rows are checked: a repeated or empty value is a 409
`constraint_violation` naming its row id, and nothing changes.

delete.description:
Delete several rows by `ids=1&ids=2` (capped). There is no way to send a
WHERE clause.

get.description:
A page of rows, ordered by `order_by` (default `_row_id`), filtered by
`filter=column:eq:value` / `column:contains:value`. Read with the workspace's
read-only role, so a row written a moment ago may take a moment to show when
reads go to a replica.

post.description:
Insert up to `WORKSPACE_MAX_ROWS_PER_EDIT` rows. Values are converted to the
column's type; a bad one is a 422 `row_invalid` naming `rows[i].column`. All or
nothing. A broken key or relation is a 409 `constraint_violation`; a full
workspace is `workspace_full`.

patch.description: Change some columns of one row by its `_row_id`.
